headline: Sheikh Hasina seeks new passport to return to Bangladesh
summary: The ousted Prime Minister has requested a new passport and NID, stating her intention to return and surrender before a court.
details: Ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has requested a new Bangladeshi passport and National Identity Card (NID) to facilitate her return to Bangladesh from India, according to a Reuters report.

In a letter sent by her lawyers at Matrix Chambers, the request was addressed to the acting high commissioner at Bangladesh's embassy in Delhi, citing the revocation of her previous documents by the interim government.
Hasina told Reuters she plans to return to Bangladesh in December to surrender before a court. Her aides mentioned that the specific date will be announced once formalities are completed.
The move comes after she was tried and sentenced to death in absentia by the International Crimes Tribunal in November last year for crimes against humanity during the 2024 student protests.
Hasina has denied the charges against her. Her party, the Awami League, is currently banned in Bangladesh.
Analysts suggest her return could either sharpen political divides and threaten stability, or potentially ease strained ties between Dhaka and Delhi.
Many of her party colleagues have either been jailed or are currently in self-imposed exile in India or elsewhere.
caption:
Sheikh Hasina wants to return to Bangladesh.

She has officially requested a new passport and NID to surrender before a court.

Ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has requested a new Bangladeshi passport and National Identity Card (NID) to facilitate her return to Bangladesh from India, according to a Reuters report.

In a letter sent by her lawyers at Matrix Chambers, the request was addressed to the acting high commissioner at Bangladesh's embassy in Delhi, citing the revocation of her previous documents by the interim government.

Hasina told Reuters she plans to return to Bangladesh in December to surrender before a court. Her aides mentioned that the specific date will be announced once formalities are completed.

The move comes after she was tried and sentenced to death in absentia by the International Crimes Tribunal in November last year for crimes against humanity during the 2024 student protests.

Hasina has denied the charges against her. Her party, the Awami League, is currently banned in Bangladesh.

Analysts suggest her return could either sharpen political divides and threaten stability, or potentially ease strained ties between Dhaka and Delhi.

Many of her party colleagues have either been jailed or are currently in self-imposed exile in India or elsewhere.

headline: Actress Pori Moni claims car was attacked after event in Dhaka
summary: The actress went live on Facebook late Sunday night, alleging a planned attack on her vehicle following a program at Gulshan Shooting Club.
details: Actress Pori Moni alleged that she became the victim of an unwanted and planned incident late Sunday night in Dhaka.
Speaking via a Facebook Live session, she claimed that after finishing a program at the Gulshan Shooting Club, someone in an 'attacking mood' shouted and targeted her vehicle.
Pori Moni stated that her car was attacked and vandalized, leaving her unable to enter the vehicle at that moment.
The actress mentioned she was waiting in the 'backstage' area of the event venue while reporting the incident live to her followers.
